title: Title backgrounds move: gradients, grain and the recording behind glass
goal: A title page's background can be alive instead of flat: a slowly drifting multi-colour gradient, fine film grain, or the person's own recording blurred and dimmed behind the words, slowly zooming, and sharpening as the title leaves. Accents like underlines can draw themselves on.
notes: User's words (2026-10-10): "the comps in the library for titles are so very bland. They look like powerpoint titles. I am wondering if we can have more professionally polished animated title screens with interesting, tweakable effects. Moving backgrounds, text that comes in, looks polished and designed, maybe motion blur, not like a template. do research on what good looking intros look like and derive how to make it easy to build these." The research and the model are in docs/design/video-titles-polish.md (READ IT FIRST: techniques, twelve style recipes, the TitleDesign/TitlePart/behaviour model that compiles to keys, renderer costs, today's gaps with file refs). Six tasks build it in order: titles-move-in-parts, title-text-by-line-word-letter, title-backgrounds-move, motion-blur-on-titles, title-tiles-play-and-knobs, a-set-of-titles-that-look-designed. This is step 3 of 6.
acceptance: A moving gradient background (two or three colour points drifting on a loop, speed knob), rendered by a small kernel at half resolution and upscaled; MEASURED frame cost in the audit with a perf note
Grain as an effect with an amount, offset every frame, that also stops gradients banding in the exported MP4 (MEASURED banding before and after on one export)

A Recording Behind Glass background: frames of the clip under or after the title, blurred (default 30 to 40 px) and dimmed (default 40%), with a slow 105 to 100% zoom; on the title's out the blur and dim animate to nothing so it lands in the real footage
Hold behaviours that keep something moving while a title holds: background drift, a slow 1 to 2% push
Paths and lines take a trim (start and end along the stroke) that can be keyed, so an underline or rule draws on
All of it is non-destructive layer styling applied at render time; playback, scrubbing and export match
A walk inserts a title over a recording with Recording Behind Glass and photographs the in, hold and out
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Pre-build review. First-time user: they will not go looking for a 'mesh fill' or a 'grain effect'; they reach these through two new title pages in the Library and the Add Title Page menu (Aurora: a drifting three colour mesh with grain and an underline that draws on; Behind Glass: the recording under the title blurred, dimmed and slowly zooming, sharpening as the title leaves). The pieces stay ordinary and editable: the background's Fill gets a Mesh type with a Drift knob, Effects gets Grain with an Amount, a background blur gets a Zoom, and lines and paths get Trim start and Trim end keys. What the app cannot deliver from the mock-free spec: a Library tile for Behind Glass has no recording behind it (tiles are stills of the preset alone, step 5 makes them play over the person's first frame), so its tile shows a dark page. Collisions: an opening title page at 0:00 normally pushes the recording later so nothing plays hidden; Behind Glass must NOT push, because the recording under it is its background, and it leaves through its own parts rather than the bar's fade. Grown-up tools: Premiere does this with a Gaussian Blur + Brightness on the clip, keyed by hand, and After Effects draws a rule on with Trim Paths start and end; here it is one pick from the Library, and every value is still a key you can drag. No mock page covers title backgrounds; the icon draw-on mock (icon-drawon-wt) names the same stroke motion Dash for icons.

Built: Mesh fill + Drift, Grain effect, background blur Zoom, Trim start/end keys on lines and paths, Draw On and Frost builds, glass-aware push hold, Aurora and Behind Glass pages, behind next-title-backgrounds-move (on in Next). Measured: Aurora 8.9-10.4 ms and Behind Glass 4.7-5.5 ms a 1080p frame (debug, alone); banding in a 1080p MP4 48 rows plain vs 24 with default grain. Finding: 1 px grain at 12% is wiped out by the encoder (41 vs 48 rows), so grain is 2 px per 1080 lines and defaults to 25%. Earlier rules applied to the new pages: Behind Glass frosts in over 0.7 s (nothing of a title shows on its first frame), its out is 480 ms ease in (outs end inside the last half second).

left rough (under the follow-up bar, not filed): a Mesh on a path or a frame's screen does not drift on the canvas (only box and oval fills drift); mesh points have no on-canvas handles; hand drawn style arrows ignore a trim; Behind Glass over a gap is a dark page; glass under 4 pt of blur is slightly less saturated than before (boost now eases in). The icon draw-on mock (icon-drawon-wt) calls the stroke motion Dash for icons; titles use Trim start / Trim end. Library tile folded into title-tiles-play-and-a-few-knobs-restyle-a-title. Tests: whole Scripts/test.sh hit the known hang (find-out-why-the-whole-test-run-hangs-in-the-mac); split run green: core 11138, render+media minus 12 Vision/HEIF/speech suites 1128, those 12 alone 118.

Aurora (drifting mesh, grain, rule that draws on) and Behind Glass (the recording blurred, dimmed, settling 105 to 100%, racking back into the footage) title pages; Mesh fill with Drift, Grain effect, background blur Zoom, Trim start/end keys, Draw On and Frost builds; Next switch on by default. Verified: TitleBackgroundsTests, TitleBackgroundsRenderTests (playback/scrub/export byte-equal; Aurora 8.9-10.4 ms, Behind Glass 4.7-5.5 ms at 1080p), GrainBandingExportTests (MP4 bands 48 rows plain vs 24 with grain), split test run green, title-backgrounds-move-walk ok with 18 real captures plus 10 neighbouring walks ok.
